newsitem.title: USA: Sprint gaining long-distance market share.
newsitem.headline: Sprint gaining long-distance market share.

text.p: Sprint Corp said Tuesday that it continues to gain profitable market share in the long-distance market, and has not experienced the adverse impact that was reported by AT&T Corp.

Earlier, AT&T said that its third quarter share earnings may fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates, and fourth quarter results could also fall short by a comparable amount. AT&T cited stiff competition in its key long-distance telephone business, as well as pressure on revenues and higher marketing costs.

Sprint said the success of its Sprint Sense long-distance pricing has helped its consumer business grow at a rate three times faster than AT&T's consumer business in the first and second quarters of 1996.
Sprint said it introduced a "dime-a-minute" rate back in January, 1995.
"Thus far through the third quarter of 1996, Sprint is seeing the simplicity of its dime-a-minute message continue to drive record sales," Sprint said in a statement issued from Washington.
Sprint is based in Westwood, Kan.
